name: Automic Vault
description: Automic Vault detects secret exposure, hardens packages that work with secrets, encrypts .env files, and monitors the tools you install with Homebrew, npm, pip, and curl one-liners.
short_description: Don't get owned by your own tools.
full_description: From the creator of Homebrew, Automic Vault detects secret exposure before supply chain attacks turn local files into access, patches packages that work with secrets, installs tools immutably, provides dotenvx-compatible .env encryption with the private key stored in the AV Keychain, and monitors new installs and stale tool config for hazards.
positioning: Don't get owned by your own tools

exposure_examples.summary: Prints a GitHub bearer token that an agent, script, or compromised tool can copy into API calls.
Turns a readable dotfile into cloud account access.
Asks the local credential helper to reveal repository credentials, even when there is no obvious token file.

founder_context: Max Howell created Homebrew. Automic Vault applies that package-management background to local package roots, command stubs, secret helpers, and monitoring boundaries for AI agents on macOS.

endorsement.quote: we needed this yesterday but i'll take it now

security_methods_and_gaps.title: Automic Vault Security Methods and Gaps
security_methods_and_gaps.description: A candid white paper on Automic Vault controls, caveats, holes, successes, and hardening work.

use_cases: Detect secret exposure in local dev-tool files such as .env, .netrc, .npmrc, GitHub CLI config, AWS credentials, and MCP config before a supply chain attack can use it.
Harden packages that work with secrets so supported credentials are exposed only to approved executables at runtime.

Expose credentials through native helper protocols such as AWS credential_process, Kubernetes ExecCredential, Cargo credential providers, Docker-compatible registry helpers, and WakaTime api_key_vault_cmd.
Install packages immutably so agents can run tools without rewriting themselves, and so agents or malware cannot modify vital tools in the local stack.
Encrypt dotenvx-compatible .env files while keeping the private key in the AV Keychain.
Monitor Homebrew, npm, pip, and curl one-liner workflows for new hazards as the local stack changes.
